sectionHeadings: 092: A mode-only or binary change is a change
1.1 The parser reads spans and infers membership from them
1.2 Git prints no header for two real change shapes
1.3 The workaround already in the tree
1.4 Why the name list is the authority for membership
3.2 Deletion is read from the status letter
3.4 What a whole-file entry means to the clearance rules
record.summary: `couple` builds its `DiffInput` by parsing `git diff --no-color -U0 --no-renames`, and registers a path only when it meets a `---` or `+++` header. Git prints neither for a mode-only change (`old mode` / `new mode`) nor for a binary change (`Binary files a/x and b/x differ`), so both arrive at the gate as no change at all: an owned binary can change without its spec and `C-001` stays silent, and a mode flip on an unclaimed source file is invisible to `C-002`. Spec 071 met the same blindness while building `delta`, worked around it with a `--name-only` helper, and recorded in D-9 that `couple` is spec 005's territory. This spec unions the name list into the parsed diff: a path git reports and the hunk parser did not register enters `DiffInput` as a whole-file change with no spans, deleted when the status letter says so, and is then judged by the same clearance rules as every other path.
record.title: A mode-only or binary change is a change
